reasoning: Palestinian huwwe with doubled w and final e, not MSA huwa. As a discourse opener ma huwwe means 'well, the thing is', often reduced to ma hu in fast speech.
ث is t in Palestinian, so ثلاثة is respelled تْلَاتِة with an initial cluster. نصّ has shadda on an emphatic ص, doubled whole as SS.
Long aa in the second syllable, emphatic ص as capital S. Everyday Ramallah word for 'that's it / done', used more as an interjection than an adjective.

In this everyday word ظ is realised as emphatic ض in Ramallah, so I respell نظارات as نَضّارَات with the shadda that is actually said. 3weenaat also exists but naDDaaraat is the usual Palestinian plural.
Word-initial hamza on alif is just the vowel: ana. ط is T; the feminine nisba ending is -iyye, taa marbuta after ي being e.
Long ii in siidi. Used in Ramallah as a softening discourse marker, 'well / look / fine', rather than literal 'my master'.
b-imperfect of سوي, third masculine singular biswa, negated with ما because it is a verb. Often extended as ma biswa shi.
آلو is a loan with a long initial aa and final oo. ح is 7 in mar7aba. Standard phone opening in Ramallah.
ث is t, and the day name ends in a long aa, so I respell التلاتة as التَّلَاتَا. il- assimilates to the sun letter ت.
shu is the Palestinian 'what'. حلو is 7ilu with i then u, the masculine form; ya salaam is the admiring exclamation.
Loanword with short u then long oo. Taa marbuta after ر is a. Used both for a physician and as an academic title.

meaning_fix: I sent you the location (to m.)
reasoning: As written بعتلك is the past tense ba3atlak, 'I sent you'. For the future the b-imperfect is needed: ببعتلك bab3atlak. lookeeshin is the everyday loan for a pinned map location.
Palestinian CiCi shape riDi, with emphatic ض as D. Besides 'was pleased' it very often means 'agreed / consented', as in ma riDi 'he refused'.
Form VII participle in Palestinian takes the min-CiCiC shape, like minzi3ij, so منفتح is minfiti7 rather than MSA munfati7. Used of a person meaning open-minded.
Initial hamza on alif is written as the bare vowel, the medial hamza of شاء as '. In running speech it is compressed to inshaalla, and the hedging 'we'll see' use is very common.
ذ in this inherited word merges with د in urban Ramallah speech, so ذاق is respelled دَاق; ق is a glottal stop. Imperfect biduu', imperative duu'.
Word-initial hamza is written as the vowel a. Long ii in the stressed syllable, final long aa.
3ashaan is the ordinary Ramallah 'so that / because'. nil7a' is the we-form imperfect of li7i', with ق as a glottal stop.
Form V with the initial vowel dropped: tnahhad, shadda doubling the ه. Understood and used in Ramallah, though in casual speech people often say akhad nafas Twiil instead.
Instrument noun mamsa7a; the pharyngeal ح before the taa marbuta backs it to a rather than e. The usual Ramallah word for a floor mop or cloth.
Both ق glottalise in speech, and the MSA diphthong aw becomes oo, so قوس is 'oos, vowelled قُوس. There is no more colloquial word for rainbow.
ذ is realised as z here and the final vowel is a plain long a, so إذا is respelled إِزَا. Word-initial hamza is written as the vowel i.
Form II passive participle with the initial vowel dropped and shadda doubling ب. Literally 'seasoned', used as the name of the eggplant dip.
ح is 7, emphatic ط is T, and the vowel is ee not ii: 7eeT, plural 7iiTaan. Everyday Palestinian word for a wall.
bi- plus 'addeesh reduces to b'addeesh; ق is a glottal stop and the shadda doubles د. haad is the Palestinian 'this', and the question mark is not romanized.
